stories.dek: The S&P 500 is at 7,725.43, up 0.28%, but it dipped to 7,693.08 — below where it finished on Thursday — before recovering. Both reasons it was up earlier have gone. Cheaper oil has faded: US crude is $94.13, down only 0.51%, against a 1.41% fall two hours ago. And this morning's strong US factory-investment figures have been handed back by the technology shares they were meant to lift. What holds the index up now is the Dow, up 0.40%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq has slipped to +0.23% and smaller companies are negative. The market is up on which shares are working, not on fresh news. Watch whether the Dow carries it into the 21:00 UK close.
stories.headline: Old-economy Dow holds the market up as the AI trade fades
stories.short: Dow carries the market as the AI trade gives it back

stories.dek: The VIX — the market's fear gauge, which measures how much protection against a fall costs — reads 15.39, down 1.79% on the day. Our feed was 34 minutes behind when we checked, so that is not a confirmed live level; two readings minutes apart agreed to within 0.2%, enough to trust the band but not the decimal. The band is what matters: under 15 calm, 15 to 20 normal, 20 to 30 nervous, above 30 the BuyTrigger ladder's buy window. At 15.4 the market is normal, about 14.6 points below that window. The day's high has stretched to 15.94 from 15.64: shares higher and protection dearer at once.
stories.headline: The fear gauge is creeping up even though shares are higher
stories.short: Fear gauge edges up even with shares higher

stories.dek: Micron ($MU) is $1,080.82, up 0.03%, after being up 1.62% two hours ago — a 1.56% give-back in a single session. The memory-chip maker had jumped on strong American factory-investment data, and at 14:30 its worst price of the day still sat above Thursday's best. That has reversed: its session low of $1,074.51 is $6.53 below Thursday's high. This is the sixth time this week an overnight gain in Micron has failed to survive a full trading session. For someone holding for years, the thing to weigh is not the wobble but the earnings: Micron reports its fiscal fourth quarter on Wednesday 30 September at 21:30 UK, and that print, not today's tape, is what changes the business.
stories.headline: Micron gives back its whole morning jump before New York lunchtime
stories.short: Micron hands back its whole morning gain

stories.dek: Oracle has sent a force majeure notice — a legal warning that something outside its control may stop it meeting a contract — to Blue Owl Capital's Stack Infrastructure unit over Project Jupiter, a $165 billion AI data centre campus in southern New Mexico needing 2.45 gigawatts of power. The gas pipeline meant to power it slipped to 1 February 2027 after regulators repeatedly refused permits. Oracle says the project 'remains on our planned schedule'; Blue Owl says its commitments are unchanged. Neither has filed an 8-K. Oracle shares are $138.35, down 0.85%. For long-term holders the lesson is that AI capacity is now limited by power and permits, not chips. Next date: a fuel-cell permit decision by 23 November.
stories.headline: Oracle warns it may delay rent on a huge New Mexico data centre
stories.short: Oracle may delay rent on a big data centre

stories.dek: Bloom Energy ($BE) is $284.71, up 6.77% — the biggest move on our watchlist today — after falling about 6% on Thursday when Oracle's force majeure notice became public. Bloom makes the fuel cells that would generate power on site at Project Jupiter while the delayed gas pipeline is missing. Thursday's reaction treated the delay as bad news for everyone involved; today's reaction says the market has thought again and decided the company bridging the gap is the one that gains from it. For a long-term holder this is the useful shape of the AI build-out: when power becomes the bottleneck, value moves to whoever supplies power. The permit decision due by 23 November is the next real test.
stories.headline: Bloom Energy jumps as investors bet on fuel cells over the pipeline
stories.short: Bloom Energy jumps on the fuel-cell bet

stories.dek: Nvidia ($NVDA) is $224.26, down 0.14%, having opened up 0.90% this morning. Its lowest price today, $223.13, is $1.45 below where it closed on Thursday. That matters because this morning's American data showed business spending on equipment — the line that pays for AI hardware — rising 1.6% in August against the 0.5% expected, the strongest such reading this year. Nvidia has taken none of it. Earlier today the memory maker Micron took the news and Nvidia did not; by the afternoon neither is holding a gain. For a long-term holder the point is not the 0.14%, it is that a genuinely strong spending number moved neither of the two names it should have moved most.

stories.short: Nvidia turns negative on a strong factory print

stories.dek: Robinhood ($HOOD) is $118.68, down 1.77%, with a low of $117.53. This is its third leg down today: it was up 1.51% at 12:30, down 0.43% at 14:30, and is now 3.24% below that 12:30 mark. Nothing explains it from the company — its most recent filing with the US regulator is dated 24 September and there has been nothing since, which we re-checked this run rather than carrying the claim forward. A share that swings three percent in four hours on no company news is usually being moved by who is trading it rather than by what the business is worth. The next thing that would actually change the business is its own quarterly results, not today's tape.

stories.dek: Europe gave away its gains all day: Germany's DAX finished around 25,386.64, up 0.48% after being up 0.89% this morning; London's FTSE 100 added 0.07% and Paris's CAC 40 lost 0.14%. These are final-hour marks rather than confirmed closing prints, because our feed stamped them about twelve minutes before the bell. Behind it all, the US 10-year Treasury yield — the government's cost of borrowing for a decade, and the benchmark most other borrowing is priced off — sits at 5.18%, its highest since 2007 and 22 basis points above Monday's 4.96%. No new reading is published until after 20:30 UK. Higher for longer here makes every future profit worth a little less today.
stories.headline: Europe drifts to a flat finish while US borrowing costs stay high
stories.short: Europe flat; US borrowing costs stay high
